_source: Eurobound-spr0. Backpack Girl Who Never Left, Absinthe Arcade couchsurf (Couchsurfing Chronicles, Debaucheryville). States 1 and 3: WritingRoom/tasks/20261112_1518_backpack_girl_one_night_stand/final.md sections 1-3 (author, Desk Eurobound-3ho-q13: Lord Pilsner, 'The Book Takes the Ring'). States 2 and 4: design/quests/debaucheryville/couchsurfingchroniclesdebaucheryville.md:148-200 with the four fixes (Desk Eurobound-3ho-q14: 'Approve all: ring stays a story beat, skip the pick when infected, apply the 4 fixes'). Every line is copied verbatim. Each segment (approach, pick, goes, cutaway, morning, rationalisations, s2_refusal, s4_sting, s4_closing) is a chain that ends; BackpackGirlCouchsurf (game/worlds/debaucheryville/absinthe_arcade/backpack_girl_couchsurf.gd) picks the segments for the four states, moves the clock to 02:40 and 07:40 between them and grants the payload once. direction, inline_direction and direction_after are the script's stage directions, kept for the record; the game never shows them (no narrator).
speaker: Backpack Girl

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Oh, hey! You look better. You look — yeah. Good for you, genuinely.
It doesn't come out of the song, though. You get that, right? You cured the verse. You did not cure the *song*. Somebody sang it in Publandia last week and I've never even been.
direction: She looks up from the notebook. She has performed the ballad, by this point, roughly forty times.
(the sting)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: The room's still a no. That was never about the rash.
direction: She strums one chord. It is the wrong string. She leaves it.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: —no, okay, no, come on. COME ON. You went to *Sinfonia*. For a *coin*. That's a whole third movement and I'm not going to sit here and pretend I don't want it.
direction: Three seconds. She looks at him, then at the notebook. The notebook wins, the way it always wins, because a man who crossed a continent for a piece of nineteen-ninety latex is not something the archive can be expected to pass up.
(reversing entirely, delighted, already shuffling sideways toward her door)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Oh — hey. Hey. You want the rest of this? I'm serious, take it. I've eaten. Sit down. You look like a story.
direction: Absinthe Arcade. She is on the floor, back against a cabinet, half a kebab in her hand, ukulele across her knees. One string is visibly wrong.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Okay. Don't say the thing you say when you meet people. Say the thing you'd say if you were already bored of me.
direction: They sit. The notebook is out before anyone has said a name.
(writing, not looking up)

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: I'm divorced.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: It's laminated.
direction: A beat. She writes.
(producing it, eager, unfolding it)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Why is it laminated.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: They give you two copies. I wanted one that would survive.

nodes.speaker: Chadwick
lines: Four hundred and six.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Four hundred and six what.

nodes.speaker: Chadwick
lines: It fluctuates.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: That's not a following. That's a group chat.

nodes.speaker: Chadwick
lines: It's a *community*.

nodes.speaker: Bradley
lines: My resting heart rate's forty-one.

nodes.speaker: Bradley
lines: I timed it myself.
direction: She stops writing.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Okay. Nobody said anything true, so I'm going to say the true thing. There's floor at my place. There's always floor at my place, that's my whole practice.
direction: She writes something long. It takes a while.
(finally looking up, warmer than the situation deserves)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: And there's my room. One bed. One of you. The other two get the floor and the common room and the book.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: The book?

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: My roommates run a book on how long guests stay. You're all in it. It's not personal, it's *data*.
direction_after: All three stand up at the same time. It is the most competitive any of them have been all trip.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: You. Divorce. Four times, you told me. Four times in six minutes.
direction: She looks at the notebook, then at him.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: It's a big thing.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: It's a *chorus*. Bring the paperwork, I want the dates.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: Bros. She wants the dates.
direction: (to the other two, hoarse with feeling)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Common room's through there. Mats in the cupboard. Don't move the mats, they've got a system.
direction: She is already moving. The pack never comes off. He follows.
(over her shoulder, to the two left on the floor)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: There's a vending machine. It's not a good vending machine, but it's *ours*.
direction: (the last thing, from the door, entirely sincere)

nodes.speaker: Bradley
lines: That's the fastest anyone's ever picked one of us.
direction: The door closes.

nodes.speaker: Chadwick
lines: It's because I had the phone.

nodes.speaker: Bradley
lines: It's because he had the phone.

nodes.speaker: Chadwick
lines: I'm going to watch this back.
direction: (filming the door)

nodes.speaker: Roommate 1
lines: Two days. I said two days.
direction: Two mats. Three roommates. One lamp. The book.
Through the wall: a ukulele being tuned. It takes a long time. Then a chord. Then the wrong string, held, deliberately, for far longer than a mistake needs to be held.
(not looking up)

nodes.speaker: Roommate 2
lines: I said one. He's got the face of a one.

nodes.speaker: Roommate 3
lines: I've got the common room, before seven.
direction: (writing)

nodes.speaker: Bradley
lines: Forty-one.
direction: Bradley is doing push-ups. Chadwick is filming Bradley doing push-ups.
(on the floor)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Don't go anywhere. I'm at the bit where you're tall.
direction: Pilsner is on a third mat, which he did not have at 02:40. His hair is up on one side. He is awake, not moving, and pleased about the mat.
She is in the doorway of her room with the notebook, mid-line, not looking up.
(not looking up)

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: I'm in the song.
direction: (to the bros, instantly, quietly, thrilled)

nodes.speaker: Chadwick
lines: The floor's where she puts the important guys. Closer to the music.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: She needed the bed. You can't sleep on pages.

nodes.speaker: Roommate 2
lines: It won't come off.
direction: Roommate 2 comes out of the kitchenette drying a mug. There is a ring on his pinky finger. It is very obviously too small.
(holding up the hand, to nobody)

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: That's my ring.

nodes.speaker: Roommate 2
lines: Yeah.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: Take it off.

nodes.speaker: Roommate 2
lines: I've tried.

nodes.speaker: Roommate 1
lines: 'Nobody hears it before me.' Ring on the table, ring's in play. You went in at one. She played it at six. In this room. To us. And the vending machine.
direction: (opening the book, reading it back flatly)

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: I was in the room.

nodes.speaker: Roommate 1
lines: You were asleep.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: I was in the room while I was asleep.

nodes.speaker: Roommate 2
lines: I've run this book nine times. It's never been a ring.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: He's keeping it warm for me. That's what he's doing. He's a warmer.
direction: (to the bros, with total conviction)

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: He can't get it off. It's not even off.
direction: Nobody hands it back. Roommate 1 closes the book.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Oh, you *lost* it. That's not a verse, that's a bridge. Twenty minutes. Don't leave the building.
direction: She looks up from the notebook for the first time.
(delighted, appalled, sincere)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: It's called *The Ballad of the Bros*. Nine o'clock, this room, there's a vending machine, and it's going to be beautiful. Bring the other two. They're the chorus.
direction: She tears a page out, crosses the room, and puts it in his hand. It is the ballad. Verse two is the aura. Verse three is him, and verse three has the divorce story in it four times, because he told it four times.
(hand on his shoulder, meaning every word)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: You understand this doesn't retire the old verses. Nothing retires. That's not a threat, that's just — that's how an archive works. Thank you for coming back. Genuinely. You're the gift that keeps on being a *song*.
direction: (over the strumming, sincerely, hand on his shoulder)

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: Bros. My name's in it four times. Four's a lot. My ex-wife's name isn't in anything.

nodes.speaker: Chadwick
lines: Four times is a lot of times.

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: I told her four times. She listened four times.

nodes.speaker: Bradley
lines: You'll get the ring back at the show, right? After the show?

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: After the show. Obviously after the show.

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Oh. **Oh.** No. No, absolutely not, and also — hold on, don't move, I'm getting the second verse.
direction: She says yes immediately — she always says yes — and then the shimmer catches the cabinet light at waist height and she stops, tilts her head, and reaches for the notebook instead of the kebab.
(delighted, appalled, and already composing — all three at once)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: *He came for the culture, he stayed for the burn / He said it was ivy, he'll never learn / O the aura, the aura, it screamed and it stung / And nobody told him — and nobody's tongue—*
direction: She does not leave. She does not raise her voice. She writes for ninety seconds while he stands there, then walks to the hostel common room across the square with him still following, and performs the finished piece to eleven people and a vending machine.
(performing, four chords, one of them wrong, deadly sincere)

nodes.speaker: Backpack Girl
lines: Thank you for this. Truly. You gave me a *whole second movement*. The room's a no, obviously. But thank you.
direction: She never once uses the word. The entire ballad is euphemism, and every person in the room understands it instantly. The vending machine is the only thing in the room not laughing. She takes a bow. Two roommates settle a bet.
(afterwards, warmly, hand on his shoulder, meaning it)

nodes.speaker: Chadwick
lines: Bros. She wrote a SEQUEL about us. That's a franchise.
direction: Bro rationalisation, immediately after:

nodes.speaker: Lord Pilsner
lines: Euromemeian artists write songs about people who MATTER. FlagMan's system doesn't even have a flag for this.

nodes.speaker: Bradley
lines: 'Subject of an original Euromemeian folk composition.' I'm putting the whole chorus in my bio.
